pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why does compost help the environment? (1 mark)
   A. It kills all soil animals
   B. It uses up all the water
   C. It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   D. It creates more rubbish

2. What is irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting crops
   B. Spraying crops with medicine
   C. Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   D. Digging the soil

3. Why should food be cut into small pieces before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   B. They take longer to cook
   C. They need more water
   D. They burn the pot

4. Why do we soak dry beans before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They become bigger than the pot
   B. They become poisonous
   C. They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   D. They dry out

5. Which animal often picks maize cobs and bananas? (1 mark)
   A. Monkey
   B. Cow
   C. Hen
   D. Duck

6. Why does a scarecrow need a hat and clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To look like a person and frighten animals
   B. To store food
   C. To dry the crops
   D. To keep warm

7. What is a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A farm tool for digging
   B. A kind of fence
   C. A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   D. A wild bird

8. Which tool is used to make the soil fine and level? (1 mark)
   A. Panga
   B. Spade only for cutting trees
   C. Rake
   D. Hammer

9. About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 cm
   B. About 1 mm
   C. Touching each other
   D. 5 metres

10. Where should you buy fruit seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. From a stream
   B. From anyone on the road
   C. A trusted nursery or agrovet
   D. From a scrap yard

11. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To water the neighbours
   B. To hide the seedling
   C. To give the tree shade
   D. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily

12. Which sign shows a purple passion fruit is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. A white flower
   B. Hard green skin
   C. Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   D. Bright green skin

13. What is topsoil? (1 mark)
   A. The dark top layer of soil
   B. A fertiliser
   C. Sand from the river
   D. The bottom layer

14. Why does passion fruit need a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. It eats insects
   B. Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   C. It grows underground
   D. It is a tree

15. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Cow
   B. Goat
   C. Dog
   D. Hen

16. Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. To make it colder
   B. To make it blue
   C. To kill germs
   D. To make it thicker

17. Which animal is not domestic? (1 mark)
   A. Elephant
   B. Hen
   C. Cow
   D. Goat

18. Which of these is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Giraffe
   B. Lion
   C. Goat
   D. Zebra

19. Which product comes from a hen? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Honey
   C. Wool
   D. Leather

20. What do body-building foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Help the body to grow and repair
   B. Only give heat
   C. Only quench thirst
   D. Make food taste sweet

21. Which nutrient do body-building foods supply? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Protein
   C. Fibre only
   D. Salt

22. Which of these animal foods is rich in protein? (1 mark)
   A. Cassava
   B. Fish
   C. Bread
   D. Banana

23. Which activity is part of keeping a food journal? (1 mark)
   A. Buying food
   B. Throwing food away
   C. Writing what you eat at each meal
   D. Cooking only

24. Which of these is a kitchen safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Never leave cooking food alone
   B. Play around the stove
   C. Use wet cloths
   D. Leave water near hot oil

25. Which food may be served with boiled potatoes for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. A second helping of potatoes only
   B. Soda only
   C. Vegetable stew
   D. Sugar

26. Why should potatoes be cut into pieces of equal size before boiling? (1 mark)
   A. They cook at the same time
   B. To make them cold
   C. To waste time
   D. To make them bigger

27. Which of these is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A frying pan
   B. A bowl
   C. A cup
   D. A bucket

28. Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Fish pieces in a pan
   B. A fried egg
   C. Chapati in a pan
   D. Mandazi

29. What should you do after coughing into your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Wipe them on your clothes
   B. Shake hands
   C. Wash your hands with soap and water
   D. Ignore it

30. What should be placed under a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A basin or a soak pit
   B. A plant only
   C. A radio
   D. A bed

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three good personal hygiene practices apart from washing hands. (3 marks)

32. List three safety rules when harvesting fruit. (3 marks)

33. Describe how to build a compost heap using layers. (4 marks)

34. Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day. (3 marks)

35. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

36. Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community. (5 marks)

37. Why must a passion fruit plant have a trellis? (2 marks)

38. State two ways of making drinking water safe. (2 marks)

39. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)

40. Why must fish be dried before shallow frying? (3 marks)

41. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)

42. State the difference between boiling and shallow frying. (2 marks)

43. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

44. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)

45. Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used? (2 marks)

46. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   It turns waste into useful manure.

2. C — Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   Irrigation means supplying water to crops artificially.

3. A — Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   Small pieces heat through quickly.

4. C — They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   Soaked beans soften and cook faster.

5. A — Monkey
   Monkeys pick crops from farms near forests.

6. A — To look like a person and frighten animals
   Animals fear people, so a figure like a person scares them.

7. C — A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

8. C — Rake
   A rake breaks lumps and levels the bed.

9. A — About 5 cm
   Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

10. C — A trusted nursery or agrovet
   Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

11. D — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

12. C — Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   Purple types change colour when ripe.

13. A — The dark top layer of soil
   Topsoil is rich in plant food.

14. B — Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   Climbers need supports.

15. C — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

16. C — To kill germs
   Boiling makes it safe.

17. A — Elephant
   Elephants are wild.

18. C — Goat
   Goats are kept by farmers.

19. A — Eggs
   Hens lay eggs.

20. A — Help the body to grow and repair
   They are rich in protein.

21. B — Protein
   Protein builds muscles.

22. B — Fish
   Fish is a protein food.

23. C — Writing what you eat at each meal
   Records help you check your meals.

24. A — Never leave cooking food alone
   Careful supervision prevents fires.

25. C — Vegetable stew
   Vegetables add protective foods.

26. A — They cook at the same time
   Equal pieces cook evenly.

27. A — A frying pan
   A flat pan holds a little oil.

28. D — Mandazi
   Mandazi float in deep oil.

29. C — Wash your hands with soap and water
   Germs from coughs stay on hands.

30. A — A basin or a soak pit
   To catch the dirty water.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, keeping nails short, wearing clean clothes, drinking safe water (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a ladder or picking pole; do not climb thin branches; wash hands and fruit; use both hands (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a shady place; lay sticks; add a dry layer, a green layer and dung; sprinkle soil and water; repeat to chest height; cover the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for place, base and layers, soil and water, and covering.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Its stem is soft and cannot stand, so the trellis supports it as it climbs and spreads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soft stem, 1 mark for support.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wet food makes the hot oil splash, which can burn people, so the fish should be dried with a cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for splash, 1 for burns, 1 for drying.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.
